**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white square plate is about 24 cm across (side-to-side), so area ≈ 24 × 24 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm². I'll use ~490 cm² as the vessel area.

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) Bacon strip, longer piece, curled; (2) bacon strip, shorter piece. A tiny crumb is negligible. No visible oil pool beyond light grease staining.

**STEP 4 - Area:**
- Longer bacon strip: ~18 cm long × ~2 cm wide ≈ 36 cm² → ~7% of plate.
- Shorter bacon strip: ~11 cm × ~1.8 cm ≈ 20 cm² → ~4% of plate.
- Total food ≈ 11% of plate, consistent with two strips.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Bacon is thin, about 0.3 cm thick when cooked and flat.
- Longer strip: 36 cm² × 0.3 cm ≈ 11 ml.
- Shorter strip: 20 cm² × 0.3 cm ≈ 6 ml.
- Total ≈ 17 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cooked bacon is dense, about 0.9–1.0 g/ml in this scheme, but thin strips are mostly flat, so use 0.9.
- Total ≈ 17 × 0.9 ≈ 15 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked pan-fried bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g.
- 15 g × 5.4 ≈ 81 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two thin strips of cooked bacon typically weigh roughly 15–20 g and contain about 80–110 kcal, so 15 g and ~80 kcal is plausible for what's visible. The plate is mostly empty, so no larger total is supported.
